Let’s dive into Chapter 4: Identifying and Remedying Common Vastu Imbalances.
Even with the best of intentions, it’s easy for homes and workplaces to develop little imbalances—what Vastu calls doshas—that throw off the flow of positive energy. Sometimes it’s because of the way the place was built, or maybe changes and renovations over the years, or just the slow creep of daily life.
But here’s the thing: Vastu doshas aren’t permanent flaws. They’re more like signals—little nudges telling us that something in our space needs some attention. You might notice them as nagging health issues, money troubles, tension in relationships, or just a general feeling that things are a bit off at home.
So, where do you start? The first step is pretty simple—take a fresh look at your space. Notice any areas that feel stuck, cluttered, or just not quite right.
Let’s walk through some common Vastu imbalances and how you can easily fix them:
First up— blocked entrances. If your main door is hidden behind furniture, piles of shoes, or other odds and ends, energy can’t flow in smoothly. Try clearing that space and maybe add a friendly touch, like a green plant or a soft lamp, to welcome good vibes back in.
Next, think about the center of your home. This spot should feel open and uncluttered. If you’ve got heavy boxes or big furniture right in the middle, it can disrupt energy circulation. Move those items towards the southwest, keep the center clear, and you’ll quickly notice a lighter, more balanced atmosphere.
Another one? The kitchen’s location. If your kitchen sits in the northeast or north, there can be a clash between fire and water elements. Can’t move the kitchen? No worries—just add some red or orange accents for warmth, and place a small water feature in the northeast corner to help balance things out.
Bathrooms in the northeast are considered less than ideal, since they’re thought to drain away positive energy. But you can offset this by keeping the bathroom spotless, letting in plenty of fresh air, and choosing light colors for a clean, uplifting feel.
One more thing to look for: mirrors facing the bed. Mirrors that reflect your bed can mess with your rest, leaving you feeling uneasy. Try covering or moving these mirrors, and see if your sleep improves.
Beyond these specific fixes, there are a few habits that keep your space in tune:
Regularly clean and clear out clutter—stagnant energy loves to hide in forgotten corners.
Use natural materials and colors that match the energy of each direction. And don’t forget to add little symbols of positivity—fresh flowers, beautiful art, or sacred objects—especially in key spots throughout your home.
Remember, correcting Vastu doshas isn’t about superstition. It’s about being aware and responsive to your environment. Think of it like gardening: you watch how your plants are doing, make small adjustments, and help them thrive. Your home works the same way—just pay attention and make thoughtful changes as you go.
And here’s something really important: Vastu Shastra is meant to be flexible. Not every rule can fit perfectly, especially in modern apartments or homes where you can’t move walls around. What matters is making the best of what you have—using a little creativity and intention to bring your space into better harmony with nature.
Over time, these small acts of care can really add up. You’ll notice improvements in your well-being, your relationships, and your overall outlook. Your home transforms from just a shelter into a real source of strength and inspiration.
